# Activation Clause

Maintains a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. It installs party operations, monitors embedded access documents and controls delivery to document handlers. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. All paths below belong to the document where this clause executes.

## Configuration

Configuration is held in `parameters`, used by the runtime at `/clauses/activation/parameters`.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by valid party names. Each party needs `lead/channel`; keys in optional `representatives` are also validated.
- `required` identifies parties whose acceptance is needed; it defaults to all configured party keys. `revision` starts at the configured value, defaulting to `1`.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies access documents to embed and monitor. `/partyAccess` is also processed as an embedded collection. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies access-check configuration. The detailed permission rules of `accessValid` are not supplied.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false` and controls additions through `updateParty`. `frozen` defaults to `false`; initialization also freezes the roster when `/partyRosterFrozen` is `true`.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. They permit selected deliveries before business readiness, subject to the access and closure checks described below.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`. A nonempty list enables negotiation operations, requires a nonempty `required` roster and requires the executing document to have a `type`.
- `admission/approvers` must be nonempty for the separate approved-admission routine. That routine does not itself establish how admission approval was obtained.

Direct clause transitions cannot change this Activation Clause; roster changes use its party operations. When negotiation is configured and `everActivated` is not true, changes to the overall clause configuration are also rejected with `NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`.

## State and access

`/activation` holds the runtime roster, approvals, revisions, terms and readiness. `/partyAccess` starts as an empty object. `Clauses Initialized`, monitored `Timeline Access Updated` events and handled party-addition requests trigger refreshes. Initial party transports remain pending until access is ready.

`approved` records acceptance by party; a missing approval is treated as unaccepted during computation. `termsAccepted` requires every party in `required` to be approved and the `termsCurrent` check to pass. The detailed freshness check is not supplied. `accessReady` and `functional` record the same access-check result. That check includes proposed additions in `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current activation revision, so pending admission can affect readiness before the roster changes.

`active` requires valid access, accepted current terms and no `closed` flag. `everActivated` remains true after the first committed active state. `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is unavailable before first activation.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is unavailable after an earlier activation.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready but acceptance or terms freshness is insufficient.
- `ACTIVE`: the activation conditions hold.
- `CLOSED`: closure overrides the other statuses.

`reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or an empty string; it does not independently describe closure. Configuration defaults do not establish values for missing observed state.

A committed first activation emits `Document Activated`. Becoming inactive through access loss from an active state emits `Document Access Suspended`; returning to active after previously unavailable access emits `Document Access Restored`. These events carry `revision`.

## Acceptance and roster changes

Generated acceptance, party-update and negotiation operations require `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be `true`. Authority is checked through `call/channel`.

`approve_<role>` accepts for the invoking party lead. Its `revision` must match `/activation/revision`; access must pass validation. When negotiation is enabled, `termsRef` must identify `/activation/terms/ref`; any supplied reference is checked. A new acceptance records the party’s approval and emits `Terms Accepted` with `party` and `revision`. Repeated approval is harmless after the guards pass. Successful approval does not necessarily activate the document. When accepting current terms produces an active state, a pending proposal is marked `SUPERSEDED` and cleared, and negotiation becomes noneditable.

`updateParty_<role>` takes `replacement`, including `lead/channel`, and optional `party`, which defaults to the invoking party. It needs no revision input, but still requires exact-document review. A lead may replace its own party; it cannot replace another existing party. Adding a new named party requires `allowNewParties`. Frozen rosters, invalid names, missing lead channels, insufficient access and conflicting contract names reject the change. Every accepted update clears approvals, increments `revision` and emits `Party Changed`; direct additions also append the new party to `required`.

Actual changes to `parties` or `required` renew the terms identity and increment `termsRevision`. They close any pending proposal as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`; when negotiation is configured, they also clear acceptance.

Approved admission is a separate route. `admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, configured `admission/approvers`, identity validation and sufficient access. It preserves existing roster entries and adds new ones without extending `required` or consulting `allowNewParties`. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; an accepted addition updates contracts, increments `revision` and emits `Party Changed` with admission information.

`Party Addition Requested` carries `parties` and native Timeline Access `accessDocuments`, keyed by party or `party__representative`. Handling ignores stale revisions and repeated `admissionRef` values, embeds the required public access histories and records `/activation/accessRequests`. Existing parties needing access changes receive `Party Access Update Requested`; each request’s `ready` value is refreshed from access evidence. These requests neither grant private timeline access nor supply participant consent, and readiness does not itself confirm admission. `Timeline Access Updated` confirms a completed access-document update; current permissions come from that completed document.

## Negotiable terms

Allowed paths must be distinct absolute paths with no empty segments or `~`. Their first segment cannot be `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`. A path cannot equal or descend from a configured `accessPaths` entry. Selected fields must exist and contain text, integer, double or boolean values.

`terms.fields` stores selected values by path. `terms.definition` identifies the initial document with those values, configured access-document subtrees, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party `readerKeys` removed. `terms.ref` identifies the resulting terms package. `termsRevision` and `negotiation.revision` initialize to `1`; negotiation starts with empty `proposal`, `history` and `outcomes`, and `editable: true`.

Negotiation operations are generated for configured required approvers and additionally check membership in `/activation/required`:

- `proposeChanges_<role>` requires a user-supplied unique `proposalId`, current `baseTermsRef` and nonempty `changes`. Each change requires `path` and `replacement`. Paths must be allowed and unrepeated, replacements must retain the current value’s kind, and the candidate document must match its document type. Unchanged terms are rejected. Replacing a different pending proposal requires its current identifier in `supersedes`; the previous proposal becomes `SUPERSEDED`.
- `activate_<role>` requires `termsRef`. For current terms, `proposalId` must be omitted and the operation performs current-revision approval. For proposed terms, both identifiers must match the stored proposal; its base reference, field set, candidate validity and terms identity are rechecked.
- Proposal approval delegates its completion decision to amendment machinery whose exact completion rule is not supplied. Only when that approval records the proposal as closed does activation install its replacement values, advance `revision` and `termsRevision`, carry proposal approvals into `approved`, disable editing and record `APPLIED`. A successful call alone proves neither application nor document activation.
- `proposeAndActivate_<role>` proposes changes and then invokes that acceptance path.
- `withdrawAcceptance_<role>` clears the caller’s acceptance for the selected current terms or proposal. Current terms forbid `proposalId`; proposed terms require matching identifiers.
- `withdrawProposal_<role>` requires the matching proposal identifier and its original proposer. `rejectProposal_<role>` permits a required approver to reject it. Both close and clear the proposal with the corresponding `WITHDRAWN` or `REJECTED` outcome.

Creating proposals, withdrawing acceptance, withdrawing proposals and rejecting proposals are rejected once `everActivated` is true. `negotiation.history` records closed identifiers, not successful application; `outcomes` distinguishes application from rejection, withdrawal, supersession and authority changes.

## Delivery guard

This clause’s dispatch policy exempts its triggered initialization delivery and recognized embedded access-update deliveries so readiness can refresh. Other installed policies still apply.

Other deliveries require initialized `/activation`, `accessReady: true`, a fresh successful access check and an unclosed document. Only then can external operations in `preActivationOperations`, or nonexternal channels in `preActivationChannels`, bypass the final business-readiness check. Generated approval and party-update operations, plus configured negotiation operations, are included in the preactivation operation allowance. Remaining deliveries use `businessReady`, whose detailed test is not supplied.

A dispatch rejection skips every handler for that delivery. External inputs are still consumed and checkpointed; restoring access or activation does not replay them. An available operation therefore does not itself establish the caller’s authority, an acceptance, an admission or an active document.
